Compute Socioeconomic and Epidemiological Indicators

Source: R/sus_socio_compute_indicators.R
sus_socio_compute_indicators.Rd

Computes standardised indicators (demographic, socioeconomic, mortality, morbidity, maternal-child health, health resources, heat vulnerability) from columns already present in a climasus_df. Run it after sus_census_join() (or any step that provides the numerators and denominators) and before modelling/mapping; it works with any DATASUS system. Column names from the census step (e.g. V003_sum) are mapped to the formula-space names each indicator expects through col_mapping. Use sus_socio_list_indicators() to see the catalogue, formulas and required columns.

Usage

sus_socio_compute_indicators(
  df,
  indicators = NULL,
  col_mapping = list(),
  confidence_level = 0.95,
  add_ci = TRUE,
  lang = "pt",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

df

A climasus_df whose sus_meta stage is "spatial" or later, typically the output of sus_census_join(). Plain data frames and earlier stages error.

indicators

Character vector of indicator IDs, e.g. "dependency_ratio" or c("aging_index", "water_connection_rate"). NULL (default) computes every indicator whose required columns are present (after col_mapping); errors if there are none. Unknown IDs give a warning and are dropped (error if none is valid). IDs: see sus_socio_list_indicators().

col_mapping

Named list mapping formula-space variable names to actual column names of df, e.g. list(pop_young = "pop_0_14_sum", total_hh = "V003_sum"). Names not mapped are looked up in df under their own formula name. Non-list input errors. Default list().

confidence_level

Numeric scalar strictly between 0 and 1: confidence level of the Poisson/Binomial intervals (e.g. 0.95, 0.99). Other values error. Default 0.95.

add_ci

Logical scalar. If TRUE (default), adds _low/_high columns for indicators with a Poisson or Binomial uncertainty method.

lang

Character scalar. Message language: "pt" (default), "en" or "es"; other values fall back to "pt" with a warning.

verbose

Logical scalar. Print progress messages. Default TRUE.

Value

The input climasus_df with new numeric columns:

  • ind_<id> - computed value (scaled by the indicator multiplier)

  • ind_<id>_low / ind_<id>_high - interval bounds (only for Poisson/Binomial indicators when add_ci = TRUE)

sus_meta is updated to stage = "census", type = "indicators" (the system is kept) with a history entry.

Details

Formula evaluation: each indicator formula is evaluated with rlang::eval_tidy() against the resolved column values, multiplied by the indicator's multiplier (e.g. 100 for %, 1000 per 1,000). Non-finite results (zero denominators) become NA.

Missing columns: a requested indicator whose required columns are absent (after col_mapping) is skipped with a warning; the function errors only if no indicator could be computed.

Confidence intervals:

  • Poisson (Garwood exact): event-count / population-at-risk rates (mortality, incidence, hospitalisation).

  • Binomial (Wilson score): proportions (%, coverage indices).

  • None: ratios with complex numerators or direct index values.

See also

sus_census_join(), sus_census_select(), sus_socio_list_indicators()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# df_census: output of sus_census_join()
df_ind <- sus_socio_compute_indicators(
  df_census,
  indicators = c("dependency_ratio", "water_connection_rate"),
  col_mapping = list(
    pop_young   = "pop_0_14_sum",
    pop_elderly = "pop_65_plus_sum",
    pop_working = "pop_15_64_sum",
    hh_water    = "V111_sum",
    total_hh    = "V003_sum"
  )
)
} # }
